## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r}
df1 <- read_csv("../data/recist_deseq2_results.csv")
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r microbes}

df1_res <- df1 %>% 
  mutate(df1_micresp = ifelse(padj <= 0.05 & log2FoldChange > 0, 
                              Taxonomy, NA)) %>% 
 drop_na(df1_micresp)
                  
df1_nores <- df1 %>% 
  mutate(df1_micnoresp = ifelse(padj <= 0.05 & log2FoldChange < 0, 
                                Taxonomy, NA)) %>% 
  drop_na(df1_micnoresp)

df2_irae <- df2 %>% 
  mutate(df2_micirae = ifelse(padj <= 0.05 & log2FoldChange > 0, 
                              Taxonomy, NA)) %>% 
  drop_na(df2_micirae) 

df2_noirae <- df2 %>% 
  mutate(df2_micnoirae = ifelse(padj <= 0.05 & log2FoldChange < 0, 
                                Taxonomy, NA))  %>% 
  drop_na(df2_micnoirae)




x = list(      Responders = df1_res$df1_micresp, 
               Nonresponders = df1_nores$df1_micnoresp, 
               Irae = df2_irae$df2_micirae, 
               Noirae = df2_noirae$df2_micnoirae)


length(unique(df1_res$df1_micresp))

#responders <- list(df1_res)

#nonresponders <- list(df1_nores)

#irae <- list(df2_irae)

#noirae <- list(df2_noirae)

```

```{r microbes}

upset(fromList(x), 
      order.by = "freq")
```

```{r}

irAE <- df5irae %>%
  select(`Patient Id`, `Date(s)`, `Attribution (Final)`) %>%
  rename(patient_id = `Patient Id`,
         irAE = `Attribution (Final)`) %>%
  fill(patient_id) %>%
  mutate(date = openxlsx::convertToDate(`Date(s)`))

 irAEyes <- irAE %>%
  filter(irAE == "Yes",
         !is.na(date)) %>%
  select(patient_id, date) 


 irAEno <- irAE %>%
  filter(irAE == "No",
         !is.na(date)) %>%
  select(patient_id, date)

```

```{r}

y = list(      Irae = irAEyes$patient_id, 
               Noirae = irAEno$patient_id)


```

```{r}


upset(fromList(y), 
      order.by = "freq")

```
```{r}

join_mdsc <- full_join(df4, df7samplematch, by = "MDSC #")
join_fnum <- full_join(join_mdsc, df6microbe, by = "sample")
join_microbe_res <- left_join(join_fnum, df1_res, by = "Taxonomy")

microbe_res <- join_microbe_res %>% 
  mutate(micrespond = ifelse(padj <= 0.05 & log2FoldChange > 0, 
                              Taxonomy, NA)) %>% 
 drop_na(micrespond)

```
Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
